Run the rmoriebricklayer command line

Source: R/cli.R
blcli.Rd

Dispatches the verbs of the rmoriebricklayer launcher:

login [--token] [--email ADDRESS [--code CODE]] [--no-browser]

sign in for the curated tables at data.rmorie.com (a free MORIE data key, issued at https://www.rmorie.com/access/): a key you paste with --token (read from the terminal or a pipe when KEY is omitted), a code sent to --email, or the GitHub device flow

logout

forget the data key

doctor

report the language-model routes available here (own endpoint, each provider with your key, local Ollama), in the order ask tries them

models [--route ROUTE]

list the models your provider (or server) offers, the one in use marked

data list

the curated tables at data.rmorie.com

data pull db/table

download one table as CSV

app [PATH] [--port N] [--no-browser]

open the analysis dashboard (rmblapp) on this machine, with PATH, a CSV file or a capsule directory, loaded; needs the shiny package

config [setup | set KEY VALUE | unset KEY | get KEY | help]

show or change the settings of the language model (llmcfg): the route ask uses and the address, key and model of each route; setup walks through them

ask [--route ROUTE] [--model NAME] [--fresh] PROMPT...

send a prompt to the model (or the named one, on the named route) and print the reply; the same question again is answered from this machine (--fresh asks anew). aye and tellme are the same verb, and a quoted question with no verb (rmbl "how do I weight a survey?") is asked too

explain-error MESSAGE...

where an error of these packages comes from (explerr), without a model or the network

bundle REQUEST...

agentbndl from the shell

wayback FILE [--out FILE.jsonl] [--jobs N] [--within 30d] [--max N]

save every URL listed in FILE (one per line; blank lines and # comments skipped) in the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine with wbsave, results in --out (default FILE.wayback.jsonl), so a stopped run carries on; wayback --retry FILE.jsonl [--include-gone] retries the failures of an earlier run (wbrtry)

verify PATH [--json] [--fail-on LEVEL] [--public-key HEX]

check every capsule under PATH as the rmbl GitHub Action does (cpschk): each file against its JSON Schema (schemapath), vrfcps and cpsbndlvrf. The secret of an hmac bundle is read from RMBL_KEY, which is then removed from the environment. Prints the Markdown report, or JSON with --json; exits 1 when a failed row is at or above --fail-on (error, the default, drift or warn). --base MANIFEST|DIR compares each manifest with its base copy, --manifests GLOB checks only the capsule files matching GLOB, --snapshot looks up each source's latest Wayback snapshot and --no-footprint leaves the footprint (co2fp) out of the report. --seen-log FILE adds the signatures an XMSS seen-log lists to those under PATH: an XMSS index one key signed twice fails its xmss_index row

drift PATH [--json] [--fail-on LEVEL] [--html FILE] [--app]

verify, then fetch each source again and compare it column by column (cpsdrft, Benford): a column past --psi-warn X (0.1) is a warning, a flagged one past --psi-fail X (0.25) drift. --allow-file accepts file:// sources, --cache DIR keeps each source and reads it when a fetch fails; the options of verify apply. --html FILE writes the interactive report (drfthtml) and --app opens it as a Shiny app (drftapp)

refresh PATH

pin each source's new bytes (cpsrfrsh) and print what changed (mnfdiff)

report PATH [--format md|json]

the verify report, exit 0; the options of verify apply

sign PATH [--scheme S] [--key-file F] [--overwrite]

pin each provenance on its first run and sign each capsule into capsule_bundle.json (cpsseal), then verify as verify does. The key is RMBL_KEY, removed from the environment at once, or the contents of --key-file, and is never printed: the shared secret for hmac (the default), else the JSON of a fipskg key, or its secret hex with --public-key, or the JSON of a pqckg key for xmss-sha256 (see the section XMSS keys). An existing bundle is refused without --overwrite

functions [PATTERN]

list the exported functions with their one-line titles, optionally filtered by a regular expression

describe NAME

title, usage, arguments and description of one function, from its help page

examples NAME

print the examples of one function

version

print the package version (also --version, -v)

help [VERB]

this list, or one verb's usage (also --help, -h; VERB --help shows a verb's usage without running it)

The launcher installed by instcli calls this function with the shell's arguments and exits with its status. Calling it from R is the same as typing the command, which is how the examples below work.

Usage

blcli(args = commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE), out = cat)

Arguments

args

Character vector of arguments, verb first. The default is the command line, commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE). An empty vector prints the help.

out

Function that receives the output text, one string at a time (default cat, the console). Pass a function that collects the strings to capture the output.

Value

The exit status (integer scalar), invisibly: 0 on success, 1 on failure, 2 for a usage error, 130 when interrupted.

Details

An option a verb does not take is refused with exit status 2 rather than ignored or sent as part of a prompt; everything after a bare -- is positional (for a prompt that itself starts with --) and only ask, bundle and explain-error accept it. A first argument that is plainly a question (two or more words, or ending in ?, with no path, line break or key-shaped word) and no verb is asked as ask would ask it.

Errors are not raised: every error is written to out as "PROG: message" and turned into the exit status. The status is 0 on success, 1 when the verb failed (an error, nothing found, no route), 2 for a usage error (an unknown verb or option, a missing value) and 130 when interrupted (Ctrl-C). The command name in messages is the environment variable RMBL_PROG, else rmoriebricklayer.

Side effects: during the call options(morie.progress = TRUE) is set, so downloads draw a progress bar; when RMBL_PROG is set (the launcher sets it) and options(rmoriebricklayer.dcache) is not, the data.rmorie.com manifest and tables are kept in tools::R_user_dir("rmoriebricklayer", "cache") rather than a fresh temporary folder. The verbs login, logout and config write the shared credentials and settings files; ask, models, data, bundle and wayback use the network, and drift and refresh fetch each capsule's source (refresh writes the capsule), sign writes each capsule's provenance and bundle; verify and report only read the capsule files; functions, describe, examples, explain-error, version and help only read the installed help.

XMSS keys

An XMSS key (pqckg) signs each of its 2^height indices once; two signatures at one index let anyone forge a third. Its private key never changes, but its state, the indices already used, changes with every signature, and a copy of an old state signs used indices again (RFC 10033, "Hash-Based Signatures: State and Backup Management", sections 2 and 4). rmbl sign --scheme xmss-sha256 --key-file KEY therefore treats the key file as the state:

  • Before anything is signed it rewrites KEY, under a lock, through a temporary file in the same directory that is flushed to the disk and renamed over it, with next_index advanced and the state in a used field: highest (the highest index used), generation (one more at every write), writer (a digest of the host name and boot id), the last reserved block and, once split, sectors. A crash after that write loses the reserved indices and never reuses one. A KEY that cannot be rewritten (not writable, a read-only file system) is refused.

  • --state-file FILE keeps the state in FILE (an absolute path to a writable regular file, or a new file in a writable directory) and only reads KEY; a key in RMBL_KEY needs it. The command line never uses the configuration directory that cpssign uses in an R session; it reads and updates the record in RMBL_XMSS_INDEX_FILE only when that is set.

  • --sectors K --sector NAME (K a power of two, at most half the indices) splits the indices into K disjoint ranges and signs only in one of them, which keeps its own highest index; the range of NAME is SHA-256 of NAME and the key fingerprint, modulo K. Two names land in one sector by chance, so for real use give each runner its own --sector-index I. A sector that is used up is refused. Once split, sign only through rmbl sign.

  • --reserve N marks the next N indices used in one write (at least one per capsule signed); the capsules of the run are signed from that block, and the indices it does not use are lost, as RFC 10033, section 5.9 allows.

  • A stale copy is refused: when a bundle under PATH, or the --seen-log FILE that every rmbl sign appends its signatures to, shows this key signed an index above what the state says, nothing is signed. A note says when another host wrote the state last.

  • When N or fewer indices are left in the range (--warn-left N, by default a tenth of the range) a warning is printed in the report and on standard error (RFC 10033, section 3.4).

A CI secret is a fixed copy of the key that every job starts from, so each job would sign the same indices again: in CI sign with ML-DSA (fipskg), or keep the XMSS state in a file that persists between jobs and give each concurrent runner its own sector. rmbl verify shows each XMSS signature's index and key fingerprint, and xmssidxseen lists indices signed twice. NIST SP 800-208 approves XMSS only when the key is made and used inside a hardware cryptographic module that never exports it; a key file is software, so this follows the software guidance of RFC 10033 and is not a validated SP 800-208 deployment.

See also

instcli to put the command on your PATH.

Examples

blcli("version")
#> rmoriebricklayer 1.0.0
blcli("help")
#> usage: rmoriebricklayer <verb> [options]   (rmbl is the same command as rmoriebricklayer)
#> 
#> Language models (your own key, or a model on your machine)
#>   ask [--route R] [--model NAME] PROMPT...  ask a model and print the reply (--fresh: ask anew)
#>   aye, tellme, or just "QUESTION?"          the same as ask
#>   explain-error "MESSAGE"                   where an error comes from and what to do, no model needed
#>   doctor                                    what is set up, and which route ask will use
#>   config                                    show every language-model setting
#>   config setup                              answer a few questions to set them all
#>   config set KEY VALUE | unset KEY          change one (keys: config help)
#>   config reset [--force]                    move an unreadable settings file aside
#>   models [--route R]                        models your provider or server offers
#>   bundle REQUEST...                         agentbndl() from the shell
#> 
#> Data and functions
#>   login [--token] [--email ADDRESS]         sign in for the curated tables at data.rmorie.com
#>         [--code CODE] [--no-browser]
#>   logout                                    forget the data key
#>   data list                                 curated tables at data.rmorie.com
#>   data pull db/table [--out FILE.csv]       download one of them (your MORIE data key)
#>   app [PATH] [--port N] [--no-browser]      the analysis dashboard on this machine (needs shiny)
#>   wayback FILE [--out F.jsonl] [--jobs N]   archive every URL in FILE (archive.org keys)
#>   wayback --retry F.jsonl                   retry the failed URLs of an earlier wayback run
#>   functions [PATTERN]                       exported functions and their titles
#>   describe NAME                             help page of one function
#>   examples NAME                             its examples
#>   version                                   package version
#> 
#> Capsules (the checks of the rmbl GitHub Action)
#>   verify PATH [--json] [--fail-on LEVEL]    schemas, digests, bundle signature (hmac secret: RMBL_KEY)
#>         [--base MANIFEST|DIR] [--snapshot]  manifests against their base copies; Wayback snapshots
#>   drift PATH [--json] [--fail-on LEVEL]     verify, then fetch each source and compare it with the pin
#>         [--psi-warn X] [--psi-fail X]       the PSI bands of the column table (0.1 and 0.25)
#>         [--html FILE] [--app]               and write the drift report, or open it as an app
#>   refresh PATH                              pin each source's new bytes in its provenance
#>   sign PATH [--scheme S] [--key-file F]     pin and sign each capsule (key: RMBL_KEY or the file), verify
#>   report PATH [--format md|json]            the verify report; never fails
#> 
#> More help
#>   rmoriebricklayer help start      getting started, step by step
#>   rmoriebricklayer help llm        every way to point ask at a model (your key, Ollama, your own server)
#>   rmoriebricklayer help config     every setting, its environment variable, and examples
#>   rmoriebricklayer help r          the same from R and Rscript
#>   rmoriebricklayer VERB --help     one verb's usage

# one verb's usage
blcli(c("help", "data"))
#> usage: rmoriebricklayer data list | data pull db/table [--out FILE.csv]   curated tables at data.rmorie.com (your MORIE key)

# capture the output instead of printing it
con <- textConnection("lines", "w")
status <- blcli(c("functions", "^drbg_"), out = function(x) cat(x, file = con))
close(con)
status
#> [1] 0
lines
#> [1] "  drbg_generate  The 0.5.x names, kept as aliases"
#> [2] "  drbg_new       The 0.5.x names, kept as aliases"
#> [3] "  drbg_reseed    The 0.5.x names, kept as aliases"

# an unknown verb is a usage error: status 2, nothing run
blcli("nonsense")
#> rmoriebricklayer: unknown verb 'nonsense'; try `rmoriebricklayer help`, or `rmoriebricklayer ask "QUESTION"` for a model

# check a capsule as the rmbl GitHub Action does
d <- usecpstmpl(tempfile("capsule-"), ex = TRUE)
invisible(cpsrfrsh(d))
blcli(c("verify", d))
#> ## rmbl capsule verify with [rmoriebricklayer 1.0.0](https://github.com/rootcoder007/rmorie-bricklayer)
#> 
#> **✔ ok**: 1 capsule under `/tmp/RtmpWuib77/capsule-1ef024850eb5`: 1 ok, 0 warn, 0 drift, 0 error

#> 
#> <details>

#> | Status | Check | Detail |

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# these read every help page, which takes a few seconds
blcli(c("functions", "json"))
blcli(c("describe", "anltab"))
blcli(c("examples", "perdays"))
}
